original.title: Becoming a Self-Regulated Learner: An Overview

core_idea: Self-regulated learners take charge of their own learning. They set goals and plan (forethought), monitor and control what they do (performance), and judge and adjust afterwards (self-reflection), in a repeating cycle.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: How do students plan, monitor and evaluate their study, e.g. online or independent learning?
Which strategies or feedback help students become more self-regulated?
Typical data: questionnaires such as the MSLQ, think-aloud protocols, learning analytics, interviews.
common_mistakes: Treating SRL as a stable trait measured once, when the models describe a changing process.
Picking one model's phases without saying which model you use (Zimmerman, Pintrich, Winne and Hadwin, Boekaerts differ).
Measuring only strategy use and ignoring motivation and emotion, which all main models include.
